tiles: Change to the SIP: read by AI alone, matches the human label
Reason given: AI pre-fill matches the human label (3 runs)
Same outcome as the human labels once the investor confirms the pre-fills (simulated)
summary: Measured on 28 fresh test messages (22 real public comments drawn at random, never used in development, plus 6 status texts) and 6 guardrail tests, 3 runs each, against hand labels. The AI pre-fills what the message says; the investor confirms app status, money taken and the reason in one tap; fixed rules then pick the reason and the fix. Pre-fill accuracy without confirmation: app status 54–61%, money taken 64–82%, reason 82–89%. These facts are hard even for people: the same labeller agreed with themselves 79%, 68% and 89% on them across two blind passes, which is why the investor confirms them. The 28/28 outcome assumes the investor confirms correctly; the user tests check that. Earlier versions that let the AI guess the reason alone scored 52–72%, so the design changed. Limits: one labeller (three passes, settled against written rules); small test set; free AI tier, with a rules-only mode if it is busy. Release QA (5 Nov): 71-case test suite covering failure messages, SIP questions, account look-ups, support, managing and starting a SIP, advice, personal data, abuse, prompt injection, off-topic and junk input: 71/71 with the AI and 71/71 in rules-only mode; UI checked on 6 screen sizes in light and dark mode, plus script injection, an 800-character word and double taps.
